scope: Independent CPU source/candidate custody and geometry audit only; not Teacher accuracy, GT quality, or tracking evidence.
findings: Preparation uses only the caller-independent old Teacher referent-support scalar and original-minus-masked scalar to rank windows; tie order is descending score then ascending row-major window_id. The union is Source 0, marked Top-3 rank order, then previously unseen masked Top-3 rank order.

Preparation computes in float64 after reading float32 Source boxes and JSON grid coordinates. The authored helper casts coordinates to float32 and rounds translated centers to float32; per-case numeric differences and legal-set disagreements are recorded and must not be treated as identical arithmetic.

Preparation records duplicate-delta and whole-hypothesis-out-of-bounds rejections without clipping. Candidate and rejection geometry, source state, positions, frame IDs, and times were independently recomputed from CPU cache metadata and old grid windows.
The sealed Teacher barrier reports 42 calls and binds them to the exact candidate input barrier hash. No current Teacher result body, reason text, or job prompt was opened.

Helper candidate order is Source plus row-major window order, while sealed preparation uses Source then marked score-rank order followed by new masked score-rank IDs; helper order must not be reused for sealed label bindings.
Helper Top-3 IDs match exact preparation ranking when masked rows are supplied with the same original-minus-masked scalar objective.

The helper's float32 round-trip rejects 6 candidates that the sealed preparation accepts under float64 source-plus-delta geometry. All six are exact upper-edge contacts in the sealed second-position anchor; helper cxcywh roundoff makes x2 or y2 exceed 1.0 by 1.49e-8 to 2.98e-8, so its strict candidate-anchor check rejects before translation. Use the sealed barrier geometry as authority until implementation is reconciled; do not treat helper legality as the sealed candidate set.
